info.title: VulnMart browser API: the platform fragment (IF-1) and the lab fragment (IF-2), bundled
info.description: Generated by scripts/bundle-openapi.mjs; do not edit. The sources are contracts/api/platform/platform.openapi.yaml and contracts/api/lab/lab.openapi.yaml. Every operation carries x-fragment (platform or lab). Lab components that differ from a platform component of the same name are prefixed Lab (see bundle-report.json).

servers.description: Same origin as the dashboards (the platform forwards /api/* to the API).

get.description:
Public. 200 when the API and its stores answer, 503 when one does not. The answer names no
store and no host: only `ok` or `degraded`. The dashboards skeleton (P-07) uses it.

post.summary: Sign up as a learner
post.description:
Public. Creates a learner account (FR-ACC-01) and sends a verification link by email (FR-ACC-02).
Needs the declaration that the person is 18 or over (FR-PRV-13), recorded at signup. Answers 202
with the same body whether or not the address already has an account, so the answer is not an
oracle; an existing address gets an email that says so. A password that appears in a breach list is
refused with 422 (FR-ACC-08). Rate limited per address and per email, 429 (FR-ACC-10). Whether a
CAPTCHA token is needed is OPEN (OI-29): the field is optional and marked pending.

post.summary: Use an email verification link
post.description:
Public. The token of the link. Single use and stored only as a hash (FR-ACC-02); using it twice,
or after it expired (24 hours, placeholder), is 400 AUTH-TOKEN-INVALID. The answer does not tell
which of the two it was.

post.summary: Use the link mailed to a new email address
post.description:
Public (the link may be opened on another device). The token of the link (WP-B). Single use, stored only as a hash, valid 24 hours (placeholder); a link that was used,
replaced by a newer request, expired, whose address another account took meanwhile, or that never existed is 400 AUTH-TOKEN-INVALID (the answer does not tell which).
On success the account's address is the new one and counts as verified, every session of the account ends (the person signs in again with the new address), reset and
verification links made for the old address stop working, and the OLD address is told by mail. Consent records and invites bound to the account are not touched.

post.summary: Send the verification link again
post.description: Public. 202 whatever the address is (no oracle). Rate limited, 429.

post.summary: Log in
post.description:
Public. Email and password (FR-ACC-03). On success the platform sets the cookie
`__Host-vm_session` (HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax, no Domain, a new session id) and answers 200
with the session, whose `csrf_token` the browser keeps in memory and sends as X-CSRF-Token. An
account that needs a second factor (every admin; a recruiter who turned it on, FR-ACC-07) gets
200 with status `mfa_required` and a short-lived `mfa_ticket` instead, and no cookie yet; the
browser then calls completeMfaLogin. A wrong email or password is 401 AUTH-INVALID-CREDENTIALS,
the same for an unknown email. An address that is not verified yet is 403
AUTH-EMAIL-NOT-VERIFIED (only after the password was right). Repeated failures are throttled with
back-off, never a permanent lockout (FR-ACC-08): 429.

200.description: Logged in, or a second factor is needed.

403.description: Origin not allowed, or the email address is not verified yet.

get.description:
The signed-in user and a CSRF token for this session, so a reloaded page can continue. 401
AUTH-SESSION-REQUIRED without a valid session.

delete.description:
Ends the session on the server at once; the old cookie no longer works (FR-ACC-03). The answer
clears the cookie. The body is empty.

post.summary: Finish a login with the second factor
post.description:
Public (the first factor was already accepted; the ticket proves it). The authenticator-app (TOTP)
code, or one recovery code. A wrong code or an expired ticket is 401 AUTH-MFA-INVALID. On success
the same answer and cookie as createSession.

401.description: The code is not correct or the ticket expired.

patch.description:
Self-service profile (FR-ACC-09). Today only the display name; an email change needs its own
verification step and is added later. Members that are not in the body are left as they are.

post.summary: Change my password
post.description:
The current and the new password (FR-ACC-09). A wrong current password is 401
AUTH-INVALID-CREDENTIALS (the session stays). A new password in a breach list or too short is
422. On success every other session of the user ends and the session id changes (FR-ACC-03).

post.summary: Ask to use another email address
post.description:
The new address and the current password (WP-B, FR-ACC-09). A single-use link goes to the NEW address; nothing changes until it is used (`confirmEmailChange`). A wrong
current password is 401 AUTH-INVALID-CREDENTIALS (the session stays; wrong tries are counted like a password change's). 202 whatever the new address is: an address that
already has an account gets the "already registered" mail instead and no pending change is made (no oracle). The same address as the current one, an address that is not
one, and (for a recruiter) a disposable address are 422. An administrator's account does not change its address here: 409 ATT-INVALID-STATE. One pending change per account:
a new request replaces the older one. A person whose invite went to another address can change to it and then accept the invite (FR-ACC-05).

get.description:
The caller's own live sessions, the newest 100, newest first (story 3.6, FR-ACC-04): a `ref` to end one by (the first 16 hex characters of the stored hash of the session value,
useless as a credential), when it began and was last used, a coarse network prefix (IPv4 /24, IPv6 /48, never the address), the kind of client
(`browser`, `mobile` or `tool`) and whether it is the session making this call. Ended, idle and expired sessions are not listed.

delete.description: Ends every session of the caller at once, this one included (FR-ACC-04); the answer clears the cookie. Written to the audit log. The body is empty.

Ends the caller's session with this `ref` (from listMySessions). The answer is 204 whether or not a live session of the caller had this ref (it may have ended
already, or belong to someone else): the list shows what is left. Ending the session making the call also clears the cookie. Written to the audit log when a
session ended. A ref that is not 16 lower-case hex characters is 422.

204.description: The session is ended (or was not live).

post.summary: Start setting up an authenticator app
post.description:
Gives the TOTP secret as an otpauth URI once (FR-ACC-07). The second factor is not active until
confirmMfaEnrolment succeeds. Calling it again before confirming replaces the pending secret.
409 when a second factor is already active.

delete.description:
A recruiter may turn TOTP off with a re-login (FR-ACC-07). The body holds the password. An admin
cannot turn it off: 409. The session id changes.

post.summary: Confirm the authenticator app
post.description:
One code from the app activates the second factor and returns the recovery codes once (the only
time they are shown). A wrong code is 401 AUTH-MFA-INVALID. The session id changes.

401.description: The code is not correct, or the session is missing.

post.summary: Ask for a password reset link
post.description:
Public. 202 whatever the address is (FR-ACC-08: no oracle). The link is single use, stored only
as a hash and expires (24 hours, placeholder). Rate limited, 429.

post.summary: Set a new password with a reset link
post.description:
Public. The token of the link and the new password. A used or expired token is 400
AUTH-TOKEN-INVALID. A weak or breached password is 422. On success every session of the user
ends.

get.summary: The consent text for an attempt
get.description:
The stand-alone consent screen of FR-PRV-01 for a candidate attempt in state `consent`: the
notice version, the exact text and its hash, the retention days shown and the company that
decides how results are used. The text lists what is recorded and what is not. The attempt must
be the caller's: another attempt is the same 404. An attempt that is not in state `consent` is 409
ATT-INVALID-STATE.

value.notice_text: This is a placeholder consent text for documentation only. The final text is written with legal review (OI-33).

post.summary: Grant or decline consent
post.description:
Writes an append-only consent record (FR-PRV-02). The request repeats the notice version and the
hash of the text the person saw: a mismatch with the current notice is 409 (the screen is stale).
`granted` moves the attempt on to `ready`; `declined` ends it (state `cancelled`). The agree box
is not pre-ticked: the browser sends `granted` only after an explicit click. Withdrawal is a
later route (P-25). What the record keeps and for how long is partly OPEN (OI-37).

get.description: The caller's own records, newest first (FR-PRV-02). `has_more` says whether more exist.

post.summary: Ask for my data to be deleted
post.description:
A learner (`kind: learner`) asks for the practice data and the account to be deleted: the request is held 7 days and can be undone any time before (FR-PRV-09); nothing is
locked meanwhile. A candidate (`kind: candidate`, with the `attempt_id` of a finished attempt of theirs) asks for the assessment record to be deleted: it goes to the company that
holds it, which is asked to decide within 14 days (placeholder from RS-H, FR-PRV-08); an approved request waits the same 7 days, then VulnMart deletes it. A second open request of the
same kind (and attempt), a request for an attempt that is not over, and a learner request from an account that is not a learner are 409 ATT-INVALID-STATE; an attempt that is
not the caller's is 404. The registry has no deletion codes yet (ADR 0055).

get.description: The caller's own requests, newest first, with their status and dates (FR-PRV-08, the candidate sees the status of the request).

delete.description:
Stops an open request (pending, or approved and waiting) before it runs (FR-PRV-09). The answer is the request with status `cancelled`. A request that is not the caller's is 404; one
that is already done, declined or undone is 409 ATT-INVALID-STATE.

get.description:
Company-level view history of the caller's own data, newest first: the company, the action (`viewed` or `exported`) and the time (FR-PRV-11). Never a recruiter's name or anything
about the person who looked; the same company doing the same thing within a day is one entry. `has_more` says whether more exist.

post.summary: Open an invite link
post.description:
The candidate opened the link of an invite (story P-26 over story P-21, FR-ASM-04): no session is needed, because the candidate may have no account yet. The invite becomes `opened`
(a link that was opened was delivered) and the answer says what the assessment is: the company, the title, the time limit, how many challenges, the hints, write-up and results
rules (OI-14, OI-15) and the expiry. A closed invite (expired, cancelled, revoked, declined) answers its state. The answer never contains the invite's address. A link that opens
nothing (malformed, unknown, or emptied by the invite purge) is 400 AUTH-TOKEN-INVALID, as for the email links; opening is rate limited per visitor.

value.title: Web security screening

post.summary: Accept an invite
post.description:
Binds the invite to the signed-in candidate (FR-ASM-04) and answers the `attempt_id` the consent screen is for (`getConsentNotice`, then `recordConsent`); the attempt is created
when consent is granted. Repeating it for the same account answers the same attempt. A closed invite, an invite another account accepted, and an account that cannot take an
assessment (not an active participant) are one 409 ATT-INVALID-STATE: the registry has no invite codes (ADR 0058). Two refusals now guide the person (ADR 0073, FR-ASM-04):
an account whose email address is not verified yet is 403 AUTH-EMAIL-NOT-VERIFIED, and an account whose verified address is not the one the invite was sent to is 409
ATT-INVALID-STATE with the field pointer /account/email (add the invited address to the account with requestEmailChange, or sign up with it). The answer never says what the invite's address is.

200.description: The invite, bound to the caller.

value.title: Web security screening

403.description: The CSRF token or the Origin is wrong (AUTH-CSRF-FAILED, AUTH-ORIGIN-FORBIDDEN), or the account's email address is not verified yet (AUTH-EMAIL-NOT-VERIFIED, with field pointer /account/email, verify it, resendVerification sends the link again, then accept again).

value.title: Verify your email address to continue.

get.description:
The invites bound to the caller, newest first (FR-DSH-04): the company, the title, the state, the expiry, the rules the candidate needs to see, and the attempt id. Only the
caller's own invites (the database policy `own_invite`); an account that accepted none gets an empty list.

post.summary: Sign up as a recruiter
post.description:
A recruiter and a pending company (or, when a company already claims the address's domain, a request to join it), and the verification mail (story P-27 over P-18,
FR-ORG-01). No session is needed; the answer is 202 whether the address is new or known, as for `createAccount`, and the known address gets the "already registered"
mail. A disposable address, a bad name or company name, or a weak password is 422. Rate limited per visitor and per address.

get.description:
Where the calling recruiter stands (FR-ORG-02): `unverified_email`, `pending_approval`, `active`, `rejected` (with the admin's reason), `suspended`, `deleted` or `none`,
the company's name, whether the current data-processing terms are accepted, and whether the caller is the owner or a member. Only a recruiter's session; anyone else
is answered 404 REQ-ROUTE-UNKNOWN.

post.summary: Apply again after a rejection
post.description:
The owner of a rejected company applies again (OI-11: at any time); the company is pending again and the earlier reason is cleared. Another state is 409
ATT-INVALID-STATE; a caller who is not the owner is 404 REQ-ROUTE-UNKNOWN. The body is empty.

get.description:
The terms the owner of an active company accepts before the company can invite (FR-ORG-07): the version, the text and its SHA-256. Only the owner (others 404
REQ-ROUTE-UNKNOWN); a company that is not active is 409 ATT-INVALID-STATE.

value.text: Data-processing terms between Acme Security Ltd and VulnMart ...

post.summary: Accept the data-processing terms
post.description:
The owner accepts the version and text they were shown (both from `getCompanyTerms`); a different text is 409 ATT-CONSENT-STALE (read them again). Accepting again is
204. The acceptance is recorded with the company, the user, the version and the time.

get.description: The templates of the caller's company only (FR-ASM-01, FR-ORG-06). A company that is not active is 409 ATT-INVALID-STATE.

post.summary: Make an assessment template
post.description:
A template of the caller's company (FR-ASM-01): a title, any of the 11 challenges, and the rules (time limit 30 to 480 minutes, hints off or on with a cost of 0 to 100
percent, resets, invite expiry, retention 30 to 365 days, write-up required or optional, when the candidate sees results, flag submissions per minute). A field left out
takes its default; a value outside its range, or a field that cannot be switched off, is 422.

value.title: Web security, junior

get.description: A template of the caller's company; another company's is 404 ATT-NOT-FOUND.

value.title: Web security, junior

put.description: Replaces every field (a field left out goes back to its default) and raises the version. Invites already sent keep the rules they were made with.

value.title: Web security, junior

delete.description: A template that invites were made from is 409 ATT-INVALID-STATE.

get.summary: The company's invites and their candidates
get.description:
The invites of the caller's company, newest first, with each one's state, dates and attempt id (the live monitor of FR-DSH-03 reads the attempt from the lab's reviewer
routes). Filters: `state`, `template_id`. Never a practice attempt or anything outside the company.

post.summary: Invite one or more candidates
post.description:
One address: the invite, or 409 ATT-INVALID-STATE (a live invite for it exists, or the company has not accepted the terms) or 429 REQ-RATE-LIMITED (the daily cap,
FR-ORG-08). Several (up to 500, FR-ASM-06): 201 with what was created, what was skipped and why (`invalid`, `duplicate`, `exists`, `started`), and what was not tried
because the cap ran out (`remaining`), so nothing is lost. Each invite mails its link.

post.summary: Resend, cancel, revoke or re-invite
post.description:
`resend` mails a new link (the old one stops working); `cancel` closes an invite not yet accepted; `revoke` closes one already accepted; `reinvite` makes a new invite
(a new attempt) after a fault (FR-ASM-05). A change that does not start from the invite's state is 409 ATT-INVALID-STATE; another company's invite is 404
ATT-NOT-FOUND. Answers the invite after the change (for `reinvite`, the new one).

get.summary: Candidates' requests to delete their data
get.description:
The deletion requests of candidates of the caller's company (WP-B, FR-PRV-08, FR-PRV-09), oldest first: the attempt, the address the candidate was invited with (the
company's own invite data), the status, the deadline to decide (`decide_by`), when the deletion would run once approved (`execute_after`) and whether the company missed
the deadline and the request was passed to the admins (`escalated`). `open_only` (default true) lists the pending and approved ones only. A recruiter of the company
sees them, nobody else; another company's requests are never listed.

post.summary: Approve or decline a candidate's deletion request
post.description:
`approve` starts the hold (the candidate can still undo it for the undo window, then the record is deleted); `decline` closes the request and keeps the record until its own
date. The candidate is told either way by mail. A request that was decided already (or undone by the candidate) is 409 ATT-INVALID-STATE; another company's request or none
is 404 ATT-NOT-FOUND. Answers the request after the decision. Rate limited per account.

delete.description:
The company deletes the record of one of its candidates at any time, with no request (WP-B, FR-PRV-08): the attempt is erased, the invite and the person's view history for
this company go, the consent records are scheduled to go later (OI-37), and an open deletion request for it is settled and its candidate told. It cannot be undone.
Another company's attempt or none is 404 ATT-NOT-FOUND. Rate limited per account.

get.summary: Colleagues who asked to join the company
get.description:
The open requests to join the caller's company, oldest first (WP-B, FR-ORG-03): a colleague with a work address on the company's domain asks to join and the owner decides.
Only the company's owner reaches this route; any other caller gets 404 REQ-ROUTE-UNKNOWN.

post.summary: Accept or reject a colleague
post.description:
The owner accepts (the colleague becomes an active member, told by mail) or rejects (told by mail) a request to join. A request decided already, or a company that is not
active, is 409 ATT-INVALID-STATE; another company's request or none is 404 ATT-NOT-FOUND; a caller who is not the owner is 404 REQ-ROUTE-UNKNOWN.

get.description: The owner first, then the colleagues in the order they joined (WP-B, FR-ORG-03). Only the company's owner reaches this route; any other caller gets 404 REQ-ROUTE-UNKNOWN.

delete.description:
The owner removes a member, who loses access at once (their sessions end). The owner cannot remove themselves (409 ATT-INVALID-STATE); a person who is not an active
member of the owner's company is 404 ATT-NOT-FOUND, as for another company's member.

get.summary: The private cohort view of an assessment
get.description:
A ranking aid for one assessment of the caller's company (WP-B, FR-SCR-07, FR-SCR-08, D-93): the attempts that ended, best first by score, then more full captures, lower hint
cost, lower active time and earlier last capture. Ids only (join them with the invites for the address); no row is hidden or marked failed, and the label says the recruiter
decides. Off unless the template sets `cohort_board` (409 ATT-INVALID-STATE); another company's template or none is 404 ATT-NOT-FOUND. Never across companies.

post.summary: Export my data
post.description:
The caller's own data as a zip of JSON and CSV (story P-29, FR-EXP-01, FR-EXP-02): the profile, the consent history, every attempt of theirs with its results,
timings, hints and evidence requests, the companies that viewed or exported their data, and their deletion requests. No other person's data and no flag value
(anything shaped like a flag in a captured request is replaced by `VM{redacted}`). Every export writes an audit entry (FR-EXP-04). The body is empty. Rate
limited per account.

post.summary: Export one assessment's results
post.description:
The results of one template of the caller's company as a zip of CSV and JSON (story P-29, FR-EXP-03; OI-27 answered by the developer on 2026-10-20: scores as
CSV and JSON, no evidence): per candidate the invite and attempt state, the score of 1000, the times, the hints used, the open integrity flags and the points per
challenge. Every export writes an audit entry (FR-EXP-04) and an `exported` entry in each candidate's view history (FR-PRV-11). Only a recruiter (others 404
REQ-ROUTE-UNKNOWN); another company's template is 404 ATT-NOT-FOUND; a company that is not active is 409 ATT-INVALID-STATE.

get.description:
The audit log in order (FR-ADM-07): entries after `after_seq`, optionally of one `action`; actor and subject are pseudonyms. Each read writes its own entry
(`admin.audit_read`). `next_after_seq` is the cursor for the next page (null when this page was not full). Only an admin with a second factor.
Every break-glass session, newest first, with its admin, reason, window, reads and review (FR-ADM-03).

items.reason: A candidate disputes the score of C01; checking the capture.

post.summary: Open break-glass access to a candidate's answers
post.description:
Opens a 15-minute session (D-94) for one candidate attempt, for a written reason (20 to 500 characters). The other admins and the owner of the candidate's company
are mailed at once. A learner's practice attempt, or an attempt that does not exist, is 404 REQ-ROUTE-UNKNOWN. The reason is kept with the session, not in the
audit log.

value.reason: A candidate disputes the score of C01; checking the capture.

get.summary: Read the attempt through an open session
get.description:
The attempt's results, evidence (flag-shaped text redacted) and timeline, for the session's own admin while it is open; another admin is 404, a session that is
over is 409 ATT-INVALID-STATE. Every read is recorded in the session and audited (`breakglass.read`).

post.summary: Close a session early
post.description: Only the session's own admin, while it is open; the body is empty.

value.reason: A candidate disputes the score of C01; checking the capture.

post.summary: Review a session that is over
post.description:
The later review of FR-ADM-03, by an admin who is not the session's own, once the session is over (expired or closed); once only. Otherwise 409
ATT-INVALID-STATE.

value.reason: A candidate disputes the score of C01; checking the capture.

get.description:
The company directory (WP-B, FR-ADM-01, FR-ORG-08), newest first, optionally of one `status`: the name, the owner's name and address domain, the status, how many active
members it has and its daily invite cap (the number in force and the admin's own number for this company, null when the global setting applies). The read is audited
(the owners' names are personal data). Only an admin whose session has proved a second factor reaches this route; anyone else gets 404 REQ-ROUTE-UNKNOWN.

get.summary: The open attempts, with the ones that wait or fail to start marked
get.description:
A-27 (work package G refresh): the attempts that are open (`ready` or `running`), newest first, with what an operator needs to see which ones wait or fail. `issue` is
`waiting` for a company assessment that was consented and not started, `failing` for an attempt whose instance the orchestrator reported as `failed`, else `none`;
`kind` (`all`, `waiting`, `failing`) filters. Ids, states and instants only: no name, no address and no result (a candidate's answers stay behind break-glass). The read is
audited with its count. Only an admin whose session has proved a second factor reaches this route; anyone else gets 404 REQ-ROUTE-UNKNOWN.

put.summary: Set one company's daily invite cap
put.description:
The admin's own cap for this company (WP-B, FR-ORG-08), 0 to 100,000 invites a day; `null` removes it and the global setting applies again. The change is audited with the old
and new numbers. Answers the company as the list shows it. An unknown company is 404. Only an admin whose session has proved a second factor reaches this route.

get.description:
The approval queue (FR-ADM-01): the companies waiting for a decision, oldest first, with the owner's name and the domain of their address.
Only an admin whose session has proved a second factor reaches this route; anyone else gets 404 REQ-ROUTE-UNKNOWN, the answer of a route that does not exist.

post.summary: Approve, reject, suspend, reinstate or delete a company
post.description:
One decision on a company (FR-ADM-01). `reject`, `suspend`, `reinstate` and `delete` need a `reason`; its text is not copied into the audit log. The company's owner is mailed the outcome of an approval or a rejection. `delete` (WP-B) ends the company and its recruiters' access at once and releases its domain; the removal of its data follows the retention rules. A company that is not in a state
the decision starts from (already decided) is 409; an unknown company is 404.
Only an admin whose session has proved a second factor reaches this route; anyone else gets 404 REQ-ROUTE-UNKNOWN, the answer of a route that does not exist.

get.description:
Accounts for user management (FR-ADM-02): name, address, type, status and roles, newest first, never a password or a hash. `q` matches part of the name or address, or a whole user id.
Only an admin whose session has proved a second factor reaches this route; anyone else gets 404 REQ-ROUTE-UNKNOWN, the answer of a route that does not exist.

post.summary: Lock, unlock, reset or delete an account
post.description:
An action on one account (FR-ADM-02), audited. `lock` disables the account and ends its sessions; `unlock` enables it again; `reset_password` mails a reset link to the account's own address (an admin never sees
or sets a password); `delete` erases a participant's practice data and account (an account that holds assessment data is locked instead, outcome `locked_instead`) or marks a recruiter's account deleted.
`lock`, `unlock` and `delete` need a `reason`, whose text is not copied into the audit log. An admin account, and the admin's own, cannot be changed here: 409. The outcome says what happened.
Only an admin whose session has proved a second factor reaches this route; anyone else gets 404 REQ-ROUTE-UNKNOWN, the answer of a route that does not exist.

post.summary: Force-stop an instance
post.description:
Destroys the instance of an attempt whatever its state (FR-ADM-04); the attempt keeps its state and clock; the owner is mailed. The answer says whether an instance was alive. Audited.
Only an admin whose session has proved a second factor reaches this route; anyone else gets 404 REQ-ROUTE-UNKNOWN, the answer of a route that does not exist.

get.summary: Candidate deletion requests the company never decided
get.description:
The candidate deletion requests still `pending` whose company missed `deletion_decide_days` and never decided (A-19, FR-PRV-09), oldest escalation first: which company
and attempt, not the person's account or the attempt's content. The read is audited.
Only an admin whose session has proved a second factor reaches this route; anyone else gets 404 REQ-ROUTE-UNKNOWN, the answer of a route that does not exist.

post.summary: Decide an escalated deletion request on the silent company's behalf
post.description:
An admin approves or declines a candidate's deletion request the company missed its deadline on (A-19, FR-PRV-09): `approve` starts the same 7-day undo hold the
company's own approval would have started, `decline` ends it now. Audited as `deletion.admin_decided`, distinct from the company's own decision. A request that was
never escalated is 404 REQ-ROUTE-UNKNOWN (the same answer as an unknown request); one already decided, cancelled or carried out is 409 ATT-INVALID-STATE.
Only an admin whose session has proved a second factor reaches this route; anyone else gets 404 REQ-ROUTE-UNKNOWN, the answer of a route that does not exist.

get.description:
Every setting with its current value, its default, whether an admin changed it, and the range a number may be set to (FR-ADM-05).
Only an admin whose session has proved a second factor reaches this route; anyone else gets 404 REQ-ROUTE-UNKNOWN, the answer of a route that does not exist.

put.description:
Sets one setting (FR-ADM-05). The value has the type of the default; a number must be in its range (a candidate retention default outside 30 to 365 days is 422). Old and new value are audited.
Only an admin whose session has proved a second factor reaches this route; anyone else gets 404 REQ-ROUTE-UNKNOWN, the answer of a route that does not exist.

delete.summary: Return a setting to its default
delete.description:
Removes the admin's change of one setting (FR-ADM-05); audited.
Only an admin whose session has proved a second factor reaches this route; anyone else gets 404 REQ-ROUTE-UNKNOWN, the answer of a route that does not exist.

get.description:
The quota rows an admin set (FR-ADM-05, OI-21): a user's, a company's and the global one. A user's beats a company's, which beats the global one; with none the limit is one instance.
Only an admin whose session has proved a second factor reaches this route; anyone else gets 404 REQ-ROUTE-UNKNOWN, the answer of a route that does not exist.

put.description:
Inserts or changes one quota (FR-ADM-05); the lab enforces it from the next request. A global quota has no `scope_id`, a user quota a user id, a company quota the company's id. 0 stops a user or company. Audited.
Only an admin whose session has proved a second factor reaches this route; anyone else gets 404 REQ-ROUTE-UNKNOWN, the answer of a route that does not exist.

delete.description:
Removes one quota row; the next level applies (FR-ADM-05). `scope_id` is left out for the global quota. A quota that does not exist is 404. Audited.
Only an admin whose session has proved a second factor reaches this route; anyone else gets 404 REQ-ROUTE-UNKNOWN, the answer of a route that does not exist.

get.description:
Running instances, memory in use, queue depth (mails waiting, events not yet relayed) and failures (mails, jobs, instances) (FR-ADM-06). Counts and states only.
Only an admin whose session has proved a second factor reaches this route; anyone else gets 404 REQ-ROUTE-UNKNOWN, the answer of a route that does not exist.

get.summary: Scheduled jobs and their last runs
get.description:
Every scheduled job with its interval, its last run (status and a fixed summary, or the class of the error) and when it is next due (FR-PRV-18).
Only an admin whose session has proved a second factor reaches this route; anyone else gets 404 REQ-ROUTE-UNKNOWN, the answer of a route that does not exist.

The eleven challenges with the facts that do not depend on a person: title, both OWASP tags,
difficulty and tier (IF-7 content). Never a flag, a placement, a test path or a hint. The key is
the IF-2 form `C03`; the catalogue file (IF-7) writes it `c03` and the API maps it. Progress per
person is the lab's listChallenges.
The same facts as the list plus the CWE and ATT&CK ids. An unknown key is 404 ATT-CHALLENGE-NOT-FOUND.

value.title: Injection

get.description:
The caller's own attempts, newest first, with their state: practice attempts as a learner and
assessment attempts as a candidate. A recruiter's company never reads this list for a person; it
reads candidate attempts through its own routes (later). `has_more` says whether more exist.

The events of IF-3 (contracts/domain-events) for the signed-in user, over SSE (FR-LIV-01). The
audiences come from the session, never from the client (FR-LIV-05). `Last-Event-ID` resumes; an
unknown or too old id gets one `stream.resync` event and the stream ends (the client then reloads
the snapshot and opens a new connection). A heartbeat comment about every 15 seconds. Without
`Last-Event-ID` only events published after the connection arrive. A `Last-Event-ID` that does
not have the shape of an id is treated as an unknown one (one `stream.resync`, as in IF-3), not
as an error. The answer is not buffered (X-Accel-Buffering: no).

X-Accel-Buffering.description: Always `no`: no proxy may buffer the stream.

schema.description: SSE frames; each `data` is one IF-3 event.

get.summary: Everything a dashboard needs to start or restart the live view
get.description:
The caller's attempts and instances as they are now (FR-LIV-04). The browser reads it before it
opens the stream, after a `stream.resync`, and polls it when the stream keeps failing. The
values are those of the events of IF-3.

post.summary: A one-time ticket for a direct stream (PENDING spike S-14)
post.description:
PENDING. Plan B of ADR 0006: if the Vercel rewrite buffers the stream (spike S-14), the browser
asks for a one-time ticket and opens the stream on a second hostname with it. Until S-14 is
decided the route stays in the draft and the dashboards use `GET /api/v1/live`. If plan A holds,
this route is removed.

post.summary: Request a learner instance
post.description:
Asks for an instance of the learner's practice attempt. Answers 202 with state `requested`; the
state then advances on its own (poll the instance, or listen to the live stream). Candidate
instances are created by the platform when the attempt starts, not through this route.
409 INST-QUOTA-REACHED when the user already holds an instance or the admin's limit of the user or the company is reached (the numbers are OI-21; practice and
assessment are counted apart). 503 INST-NO-CAPACITY (with Retry-After) when the platform or the orchestrator has no place for another instance; since v2.2.0 this is no
longer a 429. 429 REQ-RATE-LIMITED when one account asks too often (an admin setting, per hour).

get.summary: State, access and health of one instance

post.summary: Get the one-time URL that opens the instance in a new tab
post.description:
Allowed while the instance is ready, active or idle and its access is open. Otherwise 409
INST-NOT-READY. The URL carries a single-use ticket that expires after about a minute. The body is
empty.

200.description: The ticket URL and its expiry.

post.summary: Reset the instance (new epoch, new flags)
post.description:
Needs the body {"confirm": true}. Allowed in state ready, active or idle; otherwise 409
INST-INVALID-STATE (also 409 when the instance is frozen or its attempt is not running). Answers 202: the epoch grows by one and the state is `resetting`.

post.summary: Stop the instance
post.description:
State becomes `stopping`, then `destroyed`. Answers 202 for a new stop and 200 when the instance
is already stopping or destroyed. 409 INST-INVALID-STATE when the instance is frozen or its attempt is not running (for example after submit; the freeze is not undone). The body is empty.

get.summary: State and clock of an attempt
get.description: Readable by its owner and, for a candidate attempt, by a recruiter of the company that owns it. Answers 200 with the state also for a withdrawn or cancelled attempt (PROPOSAL, to confirm); a deleted attempt is 404.

post.summary: Ask for the instance of a ready attempt (the candidate's Start)
post.description:
D-80 (OI-22 resolved): Start only asks for the instance; the clock starts when the instance is ready, so the cold start
never counts against the candidate. Answers at once with the attempt (still ready while the instance starts); pressing
again, or after it runs, answers the same attempt. Only the owner of an assessment attempt in state ready or running;
a learner starts through requestInstance, and any other state answers 409 ATT-INVALID-STATE. Since v2.2.0 the invite behind the attempt must still allow it: Start moves a
consented invite to `started`; a revoked, expired, declined or cancelled invite answers 409 ATT-INVALID-STATE and cancels a ready attempt. 503 INST-NO-CAPACITY
and 429 REQ-RATE-LIMITED as for requestInstance. The body is empty.

post.summary: Submit early (after a confirmation)
post.description:
Needs the body {"confirm": true}. Allowed in state `running`; otherwise 409 ATT-INVALID-STATE.
The attempt becomes `submitted`; the instance is frozen for the freeze period and then destroyed.

post.summary: Release a candidate's results (the recruiter of the company)
post.description:
Since v2.1.0 (handoff H-355, OI-15). When the invite says `results_visibility: after_release`, the candidate sees no score and no earned progress
(`getScore` answers 404, `listChallenges` shows nothing earned) until the recruiter of the owning company calls this once the attempt has ended
(`submitted`, `reported` or `expired`; otherwise 409 ATT-INVALID-STATE). Repeating it changes nothing. The candidate and anyone else get the 404 of every
attempt route. The answer is the attempt with `results_released: true`. The body is empty.

post.summary: Cancel a candidate's attempt (the recruiter of the company)
post.description:
Since v2.2.0 (FR-SES-07). The recruiter of the owning company cancels a company assessment attempt that has not ended (`ready` or `running`): the instance is
destroyed at once, nothing scores any more, and the attempt becomes `cancelled`, which the candidate sees in `getAttempt`. Any other state (also a repeat) is 409
ATT-INVALID-STATE. The candidate and anyone else get the 404 of every attempt route; a learner's practice attempt cannot be cancelled this way. 429 REQ-RATE-LIMITED
when one recruiter acts too often. The body is empty.

post.summary: Give a running candidate attempt extra time (the recruiter of the company)
post.description:
Since v2.3.0 (R-25, C-30: an accommodation). The recruiter of the owning company moves the deadline of a company assessment attempt that is `running` and whose deadline has
not passed by `minutes` (5 to 240). All extra time of one attempt together is at most 240 minutes and never reaches past the fixed lifetime of the instance (the template's
time limit plus a margin, at most 240 minutes unless the template is longer); a request beyond that, or on an attempt in any other state, is 409 ATT-INVALID-STATE. The
answer is the attempt with its new `deadline_at`; a time warning that is due again is sent again. An ended attempt is never reopened. The candidate and anyone else get the
404 of every attempt route; a learner's practice attempt cannot be extended. 429 REQ-RATE-LIMITED when one recruiter acts too often.

post.summary: Withdraw from an assessment (after a confirmation)
post.description:
Needs the body {"confirm": true}. Only the owner of a candidate attempt may call it (FR-SES-10); a learner attempt answers 409 ATT-INVALID-STATE.
Allowed in the states `ready`, `running` and `submitted` (an `expired` attempt is first moved on by the lab); `withdrawn` is answered 200 again (idempotent, the first deletion date stays);
every other state is 409 ATT-INVALID-STATE. The instance is destroyed at once, the attempt becomes `withdrawn` and `delete_after` says when its data is
deleted (the undo window, 7 days by default). Nothing is scored after a withdrawal. `undoWithdrawal` cancels the deletion inside the window.

post.summary: Undo a withdrawal inside the undo window
post.description:
The body is empty. Only the owner of a candidate attempt may call it. Allowed while the attempt is `withdrawn` and the scheduled deletion has not
happened: `delete_after` becomes null and the attempt stays `withdrawn` (D-91: the instance is gone and the attempt is not resumed; the recruiter is
told it was undone). A withdrawn attempt whose deletion is already null answers 200 again. 409 ATT-INVALID-STATE when the attempt is not
`withdrawn`; 410 ATT-GONE when the window has closed.

post.summary: Paste a flag for one challenge
post.description:
The answer is 200 with the `result` (correct or incorrect) and the
`credit` (credited, held, none). A wrong value, a decoy, a value of another instance and a value of an earlier epoch all answer
`incorrect`: the reason is never given to the submitter (no oracle), and each of them counts for the rate limit. The submitted text is never echoed in any answer and never stored;
only the result and the challenge are kept. Allowed while the attempt is `running`, otherwise 409
ATT-INVALID-STATE. More than 5 incorrect submissions for one challenge in 10 minutes are refused with
429 ATT-FLAG-RATE-LIMITED and a Retry-After header, even for a correct value (the placeholder
numbers are FR-ACH-01).

200.description: The score out of 1000 and the per-challenge points.

get.summary: Progress per challenge (milestone, solved, hints used)
get.description:
Progress per challenge. Titles, tags and difficulty are catalogue data (IF-7) served by the platform.

A learner's practice run is sequenced (v1.3.0): the learner works on one challenge at a time, so the list holds only the challenges
that have been reached (the ones solved or timed out and the current one) and each entry carries `state`, `title`, `tier` and the
countdown fields. Challenges after the current one are not listed. `total` says how many challenges the run has and `current_key`
names the one to work on. A company assessment is not sequenced: every challenge is listed and the optional fields are absent.

200.description: One entry per challenge the learner has reached (all of them for an attempt that is not sequenced).

post.summary: Begin the current challenge and start its countdown
post.description:
Only for a sequenced practice run (v1.3.0). Starts the countdown of the current challenge: Easy 20, Medium 40, Hard 60 minutes
(the tier of the catalogue). Repeating the call changes nothing and answers the same entry. Until the challenge is begun no flag, hint
or milestone counts for it. A challenge that is not the current one, and a run that is not sequenced, answer 404
ATT-CHALLENGE-NOT-FOUND; an attempt that is not running, or a challenge that already ended (solved or out of time), answers 409
ATT-INVALID-STATE. The body is empty.

200.description: The challenge with its countdown running.

get.summary: The points on the learner's account
get.description:
The best result per challenge over every practice run of the signed-in learner, so a challenge repeated in a new run never counts
twice. `total_points` is shown out of 1000 on the same scale as the score of one run. A learner with no run gets zero everywhere.

get.summary: The three hint levels of a challenge
get.description:
The text of a level is null until it is unlocked. When the attempt has hints off the route answers
404 ATT-HINTS-DISABLED, as does an unknown challenge key (ATT-CHALLENGE-NOT-FOUND).

post.summary: Unlock one hint level
post.description:
Repeating the call for an unlocked level answers 200 with the same hint and costs nothing more.
Hints off: 404 ATT-HINTS-DISABLED. Attempt not running: 409 ATT-INVALID-STATE. Levels unlock in order (2 needs 1, 3 needs 1 and 2); an early level is 409 ATT-INVALID-STATE and nothing is unlocked. The body is empty.

get.summary: The captured requests of an attempt (redacted)
get.description:
For a reviewer (a recruiter of the owning company for a candidate attempt, the owner for a learner
attempt). Bodies are capped at 8 KiB and redacted before storage. Whether a candidate sees their own
evidence is OI-15.

get.summary: Integrity signals of an attempt (evidence for a human)
get.description:
Never an automatic fail (FR-ACH-06). Same readers as the evidence. A reader who is the owner of a learner attempt (not a recruiter)
does not see the flags of type decoy or sharing, because they would tell the owner why a submitted value was not correct (the oracle rule of submitFlag).

post.summary: Record the review decision on an integrity flag
post.description:
accept: the evidence is judged fine (a held capture it points to is credited). reject: the evidence
is judged a real problem (a held capture stays out of the score). One decision per flag; a second
answers 409 ATT-INVALID-STATE. Who may decide is OI-38 (the mock allows a recruiter of the owning
company only). The decision is audited by the platform.

get.description: Score, time, per-challenge results and the number of open integrity flags. Same readers as the evidence.

get.summary: Ordered list of what happened in an attempt
get.description:
Sorted by the key (epoch, seq) of the event, oldest first, so a late event of an earlier epoch sits before the newer ones.
Cursor-paged: pass `next_cursor` as `cursor` to get the entries after the last one already read. Entries are neither skipped
nor repeated when a late event with a smaller key is stored between two page requests; such an event is shown only when the
client reads again from the start (cursor left out). A cursor that is not one we made is 422 with field /query/cursor.
Since v2.0.0 the time warnings the attempt received are entries too (`attempt.time_warning` with `minutes_left`), so the recruiter's report shows when the candidate was told time was running out.

Password.description:
At least 12 and at most 128 characters (a proposal, FR-ACC-08 leaves the quality rules to be tuned;
see the open points). Never in a log or an answer. A password in a breach list is refused with 422.

Token.description: A link token, URL-safe, single use, stored only as a hash.

MfaCode.description: A six digit authenticator code, or one recovery code (ten Base32 characters).

age_declaration.description: The person declares to be 18 or over (FR-ACC-01, FR-PRV-13). Only `true` is accepted.

captcha_token.description: PENDING OI-29 (whether learner signup needs a CAPTCHA). Optional until decided.

account_type.description: The account types of the architecture (04 section 2.1). A participant acts as a learner on a practice attempt and as a candidate on an assessment attempt.

idle_expires_at.description: When the session ends if nothing happens (30 minutes, admin 15; FR-ACC-04).

absolute_expires_at.description: When the session ends whatever happens (12 hours; FR-ACC-04).

decision.description: A withdrawal adds the value `withdrawn` (no route writes it yet; deletion requests, story P-25, delete the record instead).

DeletionRequestCreate.description: A candidate request names the attempt; a learner request does not.

status.description: A learner request stays `pending` until it runs; a candidate request is `pending` until the company decides, then `approved` (waiting) or `declined`.

SessionRef.description: A handle for one of the caller's sessions: the first 16 hex characters of the stored hash of the session value.

ip_trunc.description: A network prefix (IPv4 /24, IPv6 /48), never the address.

current.description: This is the session making the call.

token.description: The token of the invite link (the company prefix and the secret); never logged.

cohort_board.description: Turns the private cohort view on for this assessment (D-93). Off when left out.
The private cohort view is on for this assessment (D-93).

candidate_email.description: The address the candidate was invited with (the company's own invite data); null when the invite is gone.

escalated.description: The company did not decide by `decide_by` and the request was passed to the admins.

invite_cap.description: The daily invite cap in force (the admin's own number for the company, else the global setting).

invite_cap_override.description: The admin's own number for this company; null when the global setting applies.

instance_state.description: What the orchestrator last reported for the instance, or null when nothing was reported.

memory.description: Null when this process has no lab to ask.

owasp_2021.description: The OWASP Top 10 2021 category, or null when the challenge has none (IF-7).

state.description: The ten attempt states of the architecture (04 section 10.1); the same as IF-2 and IF-3.
The ten instance states of IF-5 (identical in IF-2 and IF-3).

error_code.description: An INST-* code while the state is failed, otherwise null.

Problem.description:
The error body of IF-8 (contracts/errors/problem.schema.json), copied here so the fragment is
self-contained; scripts/check_platform_contract.py fails when the two differ. RFC 9457 members
type, title and status plus code, request_id and, for 422, field or errors. Closed.

title.description: The registry's fixed generic text for the code.

field.description: One JSON Pointer to the offending field (empty string for the whole body).

errors.description: For 422 with several problems: one entry per offending field. The detail is a fixed generic text and never repeats the submitted value.

Cursor.description:
Opaque. base64url (no padding) of a text that holds the direction (f, forward) and the key (epoch, seq) of the last
entry already read. Clients must not build or change one. A cursor that is not one of ours is 422 with field /query/cursor.

State.description: The instance state machine, identical to IF-5 (FR-INS-07). Only the orchestrator writes it.

Milestone.description: Best milestone reached; none, M1 found, M2 working exploit evidence, M3 flag captured.

FlagResult.description:
What the submitter is told. Only two answers exist: `correct` and `incorrect`. A wrong value, a decoy,
a value of another instance and a value of an earlier epoch all answer `incorrect`, so the answer
cannot be used as an oracle (a probe learns nothing about what a wrong value was). The detailed reason is
kept on the server for the integrity review and is never sent to the submitter.

ErrorCode.description:
Code of a failed instance, `INST-` plus upper-case words (for example INST-HEALTH-TIMEOUT), the same
form as IF-5 and the registry. This is not the code of a problem answer; see Problem.

Instance.description: What the browser may know of an instance. Closed on purpose; no host, address, flag or key.

error_code.description: Set while the state is failed, otherwise null.

url.description: One-time URL on the instance host (architecture 03 section 3). Single use. The ticket is payload.signature (two base64url parts joined by a dot, contracts/edge/gate-ticket.md section 2).

delete_after.description: Optional. Present only while the attempt is `withdrawn` (the end of the undo window when the deletion is scheduled, null once the withdrawal was undone). Absent in every other state.

results_released.description: Optional (v2.1.0). Only on a company assessment whose invite says `after_release`; true once the recruiter released the results. Absent otherwise.

server_time.description: The server clock; the browser timer is cosmetic (FR-SES-02).

flag.description: The pasted text. Never echoed, never stored.

credit.description: credited for a correct value that passed the activity check, held when it did not (FR-ACH-02), none otherwise.

held.description: A capture waits for a human decision and is not counted.

hints_available.description: False when the attempt has hints off.

brief.description: Optional. What the challenge is about, in a few plain words (the catalogue text; never a flag).

start.description: Optional. How to begin, for example the demo account to sign in with and where to look. The accounts are documented demo accounts of the lab shop, not real credentials.

write_up.description: Optional. Present only for the owner of a practice attempt once the challenge is captured (M3) or timed out; never in an assessment. The weakness and the fix.

state.description:
Optional (a sequenced practice run only, v1.3.0). `ready`: the current challenge, not begun. `active`: begun, the countdown runs.
`solved`: captured (or held for review). `expired`: the time ran out; nothing counts for it any more.

title.description: Optional (sequenced run). The catalogue title of the challenge.

tier.description: Optional (sequenced run). The tier of the catalogue; it sets the time (Easy 20, Medium 40, Hard 60 minutes).

time_limit_seconds.description: Optional (sequenced run). The time the challenge has once begun.

opened_at.description: Optional (sequenced run). When the challenge was begun; null before.

expires_at.description: Optional (sequenced run). When the countdown ends; null before the challenge is begun.

seconds_left.description: Optional (sequenced run). Seconds left when the answer was made; null unless the challenge is `active`. The browser counts down from it.

has_more.description: Always false here; the list is complete and has a fixed size (not truncated).

total.description: Optional (sequenced run). How many challenges the run has in all, so the browser can show "3 of 11" without listing the ones ahead.

current_key.description: Optional (sequenced run). The challenge to work on now; null when every challenge is solved or timed out.

server_time.description: Optional (sequenced run). The server clock when the answer was made.

best_points.description: The best net points of this challenge over all runs (the points of one challenge

total_points.description: The best points of every challenge added up and shown out of 1000

runs.description: How many practice runs the learner has started.

cost_pct.description: Cost as a percentage of the challenge points; 0 for a learner (placeholder 10, 20, 30 for a candidate).

text.description: Null until unlocked. A hint never reveals a flag (FR-HNT-01).

has_more.description: Always false here; the list is complete and has a fixed size (not truncated).

body.description: Redacted request body, at most 8 KiB (FR-DET-03); null when there was none.

has_more.description: True when more entries exist than limit allowed in this answer (the answer is truncated). The entries are the oldest first.

held.description: A held capture is linked to this flag and stays out of the score until decided.

has_more.description: True when more entries exist than limit allowed in this answer (the answer is truncated). The entries are the oldest first.

technique_label.description: An estimate (FR-DET-07), never changes points; null when unknown.

minutes_left.description: Optional (v2.0.0). Only on `attempt.time_warning`, how many minutes the attempt had left when the warning went out (the default rules warn at 15 and at 5).

Timeline.description:
One page of the timeline, sorted by the key (epoch, seq) of the event, oldest first. The key is not part of
an entry; it is inside the cursor. The cursor only moves forward.

has_more.description: True when entries with a larger key exist after this page. Exactly when next_cursor is not null.

next_cursor.description:
Null on the last page. Otherwise pass it as `cursor` to get the entries after the last one of this page.
It never goes back: an event that arrives late with a smaller key than the cursor is not in the following
pages; read again from the start (cursor left out) to see it.

Accepted.description: Accepted. The same answer whether or not the address has an account.

value.title: Sign in to continue.

SessionOrPasswordFailed.description: No valid session (AUTH-SESSION-REQUIRED), or the password given is not correct (AUTH-INVALID-CREDENTIALS).

value.title: The email address or password is not correct.
Sign in to continue.

value.title: The email address or password is not correct.

TokenInvalid.description: The link was used or has expired. AUTH-TOKEN-INVALID.

value.title: This link is no longer valid.

CsrfFailed.description: The CSRF token or the Origin is wrong. AUTH-CSRF-FAILED or AUTH-ORIGIN-FORBIDDEN.

value.title: The request could not be verified.

OriginForbidden.description: The Origin is not the dashboard origin. AUTH-ORIGIN-FORBIDDEN.

value.title: The request origin is not allowed.

NotFound.description: Not found, or not yours (the same answer). ATT-NOT-FOUND or ATT-CHALLENGE-NOT-FOUND.

value.title: Attempt not found.

value.title: This action is not allowed in the attempt's current state.

value.title: The second factor cannot be changed in its current state.

ConsentConflict.description: The notice the person saw is not the current one (ATT-CONSENT-STALE), or the attempt is not in state consent (ATT-INVALID-STATE).

This action is not allowed in the attempt's current state.

InviteConflict.description: The invite is closed or taken, or this account cannot accept it (not an active, verified participant, or not the address the invite was sent to) (ATT-INVALID-STATE).

value.title: This action is not allowed in the attempt's current state.

CompanyNotFound.description: Not found: a template or invite of another company or none at all (ATT-NOT-FOUND), or the caller is not a recruiter, or not the owner where the owner is needed (REQ-ROUTE-UNKNOWN, the answer of a route that does not exist).

value.title: Attempt not found.

CompanyConflict.description: The company is not active, the terms are not accepted, the invite or template is in a state this change does not start from (ATT-INVALID-STATE), or the terms text changed (ATT-CONSENT-STALE).

value.title: This action is not allowed in the attempt's current state.

AccountConflict.description: An administrator's account does not change its address here (ATT-INVALID-STATE).

value.title: This action is not allowed in the attempt's current state.

DeletionConflict.description: The caller already has an open request of this kind, the request is not open any more, the attempt is not over, or the account is not a learner (ATT-INVALID-STATE).

value.title: This action is not allowed in the attempt's current state.

AdminNotFound.description: Not found: no such company, account, attempt, setting or quota, or the caller is not an admin with a second factor (the same answer, REQ-ROUTE-UNKNOWN).

value.title: Route not found.

AdminConflict.description: The change does not start from the state it is asked for (a company already decided, an account not active), or it names an admin account or the admin's own (ATT-INVALID-STATE).

value.title: This action is not allowed in the attempt's current state.

ChallengeNotFound.description: There is no challenge with this key. ATT-CHALLENGE-NOT-FOUND.

value.title: Challenge not found.

TooLarge.description: The body is over 64 KiB. REQ-TOO-LARGE.

value.title: The request body is too large.

UnsupportedMedia.description: The body is not JSON. REQ-UNSUPPORTED-MEDIA-TYPE.

value.title: The request must be JSON.

Invalid.description: A value is not valid. REQ-VALIDATION, with `field` or `errors` (never the submitted value).

value.title: The request is not valid.

RateLimited.description: Too many requests. REQ-RATE-LIMITED, with Retry-After.

value.title: Too many requests. Try again later.

InstanceAccepted.description: Accepted. The instance advances on its own.

Gone.description: PROPOSAL, to confirm. The attempt is withdrawn or cancelled, so its derived data is no longer served (ATT-GONE). getAttempt still answers 200 with the state; a deleted attempt answers 404 like a missing one.

MethodNotAllowed.description: The path exists but not for this method. REQ-METHOD-NOT-ALLOWED with an Allow header. Any path can answer it.

Unavailable.description: No instance can be started right now (the platform is at its limit or the orchestrator has no capacity). INST-NO-CAPACITY with Retry-After; try again later. Since v2.2.0.

PageLimit.name: limit
PageLimit.description: Most entries in the answer. Default 50, maximum 100; a larger value is 422 REQ-VALIDATION with field /limit. When more exist, has_more is true.

Limit.name: limit
Limit.description: Page size of the timeline. Default 50, maximum 200; a larger value is 422 REQ-VALIDATION with field /query/limit.

ListLimit.name: limit
ListLimit.description: Most entries in the answer. Default 100, maximum 100; a larger value is 422 REQ-VALIDATION with field /query/limit. When more exist, has_more is true.

Sign in to continue.
The code is not correct.

SessionCookie.description:

sessionCookie.name: __Host-vm_session
sessionCookie.description: HttpOnly session cookie set by the login route of this file (P-12).

csrfHeader.name: X-CSRF-Token
csrfHeader.description: The CSRF token, a signed, session-bound value (HMAC of the session id with a server secret; decided 2026-10-09, ADR 0019 M2), given in the session answer (`csrf_token`) and checked together with the Origin check and, where the browser sends it, Sec-Fetch-Site.
